thread:
olivia: FYI AcmeCorp is seeing weird behavior on their browser integration during onboarding. They spin up ~40 workers and observe a flood of OPTIONS (preflight) followed by intermittent 401s on POST /v1/generate. Opening thread so CS + infra can coordinate.

ken: Any details on token strategy? ephemeral per worker or shared?

olivia: They mint a fresh ephemeral token per worker (TTL ~30s) from their auth endpoint which sits behind their CDN. They said requests succeed if workers < ~10.

sam: Classic fanout + short TTL. OPTIONS spikes count against our edge rate-limits sometimes, depending on proxy behavior. Also if preflight happens and POST hits after token expiration -> 401.

maria: This account is in a renewal conversation; we need a fast mitigation path and clear guidance to avoid churn. Can ops do a temporary config tweak while we get them to change client?

ken: I'll pull edge aggregates for acme id=acme-231 for the window around when they saw the spike. @deploy-bot please summarize OPTIONS vs POST 401 counts.

deploy-bot: Querying edge logs for customer=acme-231 between 1798765200-1798765800. Summary: OPTIONS total=312; OPTIONS 4xx=14; POST /v1/generate 401=31. Peak: 45 OPTIONS in 30s window.

olivia: Matches their repro. They attached a trace with `POST /auth/ephemeral 200`, then many `OPTIONS /v1/generate 204` and some `POST /v1/generate 401`.

sam: Short-term plan I'll suggest to customer:
1) reuse a single ephemeral token across workers for the user session (avoid per-worker minting),
2) increase ephemeral token TTL to >= 90s during onboarding,
3) add randomized startup splay for workers so preflight doesn't synchronize,
4) implement a small retry on POST when receiving 401 for the first attempt (eg 150-300ms jittered retry).

ken: On our side, I can temporarily relax the preflight bucket for their org for 48h while they roll the client changes. That should reduce 429 noise. Maria, can we offer this as a one-time onboarding accommodation?

maria: Yes, we can. I'll confirm with the customer that we will bump the threshold for 48 hours and they must implement the client changes during that window. I'll schedule a 30-min enablement call.

olivia: Customer replied: "We can change client in 90 minutes. TTL bump would be great."

ken: Applying temp config now. @deploy-bot when done plz confirm.

deploy-bot: Applied: org=acme-231 preflight_rate_multiplier=3 until 1798851200 (48h). Change by ken.

olivia: After change Acme reports OPTIONS count the same but 429s dropped and 401s fell from ~30 -> 6 in the next 30m.

sam: Good signal. I'll push a short code example for them to copy into their onboarding kit:
```
// single token per session + startup splay
async function bootWorkers(workers) {
  const token = await fetch('/auth/ephemeral').then(r=>r.text());
  await Promise.all(workers.map((w,i)=>{
    const delay = Math.random()*250 + i*40;
    return new Promise(res=>setTimeout(res, delay)).then(()=> init(w, token));
  }));
}
```

ken: Ops note: we should instrument preflight-to-post latency and ephemeral-token-age at the edge for a short period to see how often POST arrives after token issuance > TTL. I'll spin that up as a short metric.

maria: I'll add a renewal playbook note: "If customer shows preflight fanout + ephemeral tokens, propose TTL extension + token reuse + splay. Offer temp preflight bump for onboarding window and a short enablement call."

olivia: I'll follow up post-call to confirm code changes and close the loop. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

sam: I'll also add a small section to the public onboarding quickstart about ephemeral token patterns and worker splay so future customers avoid this.

ken: Marking this as resolved for now; will reopen if 401/429 rates spike after the 48h window.

maria: Customer flagged as healthy for renewal pending the enablement session outcome.

olivia: Closing thread after enablement and docs PR."
